$comment: task-infra-seo-gates — Lighthouse CI gate for apps/landing (cheekycheese.tech). Used by .github/workflows/lighthouse.yml for both the mobile and desktop matrix legs; desktop applies --collect.settings.preset=desktop as a CLI override (see workflow comment). Thresholds: 0.90 on all four categories per owner requirement — a regression below this red-flags the PR, it does not silently pass. aggregationMethod MUST stay 'median' (owner requirement: median of N runs) — @lhci/utils/src/assertions.js defaults minScore assertions to aggregationMethod 'optimistic', which takes the BEST of the N runs (Math.max), not the median; verified empirically (3 local runs scored 85/86/92 on performance — 'optimistic' silently passed a 0.9 threshold on the max value 0.92, 'median' correctly evaluates against 86). Do not remove this key assuming it is redundant with numberOfRuns. Do NOT pin settings.throttling here to 'stabilize' the mobile leg: an explicit throttling object would deep-merge over the desktop leg's --collect.settings.preset=desktop and silently run desktop with mobile throttling; the mobile defaults under throttlingMethod=simulate are already fixed constants (rttMs 150 / throughputKbps 1638.4 / cpuSlowdownMultiplier 4), so pinning them adds no stability — runner CPU variance is absorbed by numberOfRuns + median instead.

collect.$comment: Explicit url list disables LHCI's file-path autodiscovery (which would also score 404.html — a page that is CORRECTLY noindex and thus can never pass categories:seo>=0.9). localhost port is substituted by LHCI's static server at runtime. Add prerendered vacancy URLs here only if a stable fixture vacancy ever exists at CI build time.
collect.$comment:numberOfRuns: 3 -> 5 on 2026-07-24: shared GitHub runners occasionally produce a single outlier run (performance 0.38-0.4 while the rest score 0.9+; e.g. actions run 30093375724, mobile leg) — with 3 runs one outlier plus one mediocre run drags the median below 0.9, with 5 runs the median tolerates up to 2 bad runs. Cost: +2 runs x 2 URLs ≈ +1.5-2 min per matrix leg (legs run in parallel); workflow timeout-minutes raised 10 -> 15 to match.
